title: Geometric regularity over a separable algebraic extension
statement: Let $k\subseteq k'$ be a separable algebraic field extension [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and let $R$ be a $k'$-algebra which is a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], regarded also as a $k$-algebra by restriction along $k\subseteq k'$. Then $R$ is geometrically regular over $k$ if and only if it is geometrically regular over $k'$; geometric regularity is the notion in [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

proof.text: ($\Leftarrow$) Assume $R$ is geometrically regular over $k'$. $R$ is Noetherian by hypothesis, so by the definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] it suffices to show that $L\otimes_kR$ is regular for every finite purely inseparable field extension $L/k$. For such $L$, the ring $L'=k'\otimes_kL$ is a field and a finite purely inseparable extension of $k'$ via $c\mapsto c\otimes1$ [lem-weil-pbc-separable-tensor-purely-inseparable-field]. The isomorphism $R\otimes_{k'}(k'\otimes_kL)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\otimes_kL$, $r\otimes(c\otimes x)\mapsto cr\otimes x$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change], together with the symmetry of the tensor product, identifies $L\otimes_kR$ with $L'\otimes_{k'}R$, which is regular because $R$ is geometrically regular over $k'$ and $L'/k'$ is finite purely inseparable. Hence $R$ is geometrically regular over $k$.

($\Rightarrow$, reduction to finite extensions) Assume $R$ is geometrically regular over $k$. Let $(k_i)_{i\in I}$ be the family of subfields $k\subseteq k_i\subseteq k'$ with $\dim_kk_i<\infty$. It is directed (the subfield generated by $k_i\cup k_j$ is generated over $k$ by a $k$-basis of $k_j$, each element algebraic over $k_i$, so it is finite over $k_i$, hence over $k$) and its union is $k'$ (every $\alpha\in k'$ is algebraic over $k$, so $\alpha\in k(\alpha)$, which is finite over $k$). Each $k_i/k$ is finite and separable algebraic, since every element of $k_i\subseteq k'$ has a separable minimal polynomial over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. $R$ is a $k_i$-algebra through $k_i\subseteq k'$, and its $k$-algebra structure is the restriction of this one. If the finite separable case below (Steps 3 to 5, applied to $k\subseteq k_i$) shows that $R$ is geometrically regular over each $k_i$, then $R$ is geometrically regular over $k'=\bigcup_ik_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-over-subfields]. So we may assume $k'/k$ finite separable.

proof.text: (Finite separable case: the base change $R\otimes_kk'$) Let $k'/k$ be finite separable, and put $B=R\otimes_kk'$, a $k'$-algebra through the second factor. As an $R$-module $B$ is free of rank $\dim_kk'<\infty$, so $B$ is a Noetherian ring [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian]. $B$ is geometrically regular over $k'$: for a finite purely inseparable extension $L'/k'$, the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] gives $L'\otimes_{k'}B=L'\otimes_{k'}(k'\otimes_kR)\cong L'\otimes_kR$; the extension $L'/k$ is finite (as $L'/k'$ and $k'/k$ are), hence finitely generated, so $L'\otimes_kR$ is regular because $R$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $k$ [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions]. By the definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], $B$ is geometrically regular over $k'$ ('a base change of $R$ to $k'$').

proof.text: (The map $B\to R$ is smooth) Let $\iota:k'\to R$ be the structure map and $\pi:B=R\otimes_kk'\to R$, $r\otimes c\mapsto\iota(c)r$, a homomorphism of $k'$-algebras ($k'$ acting on $B$ through the second factor). Let $\mu:k'\otimes_kk'\to k'$ be the multiplication and $f:k'\otimes_kk'\to B$, $x\otimes y\mapsto\iota(x)\otimes y$. Then $\pi$ is the base change of $\mu$ along $f$: by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change], $B\cong R\otimes_{k'}(k'\otimes_kk')$ ($k'$ acting on the first factor of $k'\otimes_kk'$) compatibly with $f$, hence $B\otimes_{k'\otimes_kk'}k'\cong R\otimes_{k'}\bigl((k'\otimes_kk')\otimes_{k'\otimes_kk'}k'\bigr)\cong R\otimes_{k'}k'\cong R$, and on $r\otimes c\otimes1$ this composite is $\iota(c)r=\pi(r\otimes c)$. Since $k'/k$ is finite separable, $\mu$ is etale, in particular smooth [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-multiplication-etale]; a base change of a smooth ring map is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition, clause (1)]. Hence $\pi:B\to R$ is a smooth ring map.

proof.text: (Conclusion) $\pi:B\to R$ is a smooth homomorphism of $k'$-algebras, $B$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $k'$ (Step 3). By ascent of geometric regularity along smooth ring maps over the field $k'$ [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-smooth-ascent], $R$ is geometrically regular over $k'$. With Step 2 this proves ($\Rightarrow$) for every separable algebraic $k'/k$, and with Step 1 the lemma.
